User: How far up the row of the knuckles do you go? How can one keep the string on his fingertip? These are questions starting archers ask. It looks easy when you look at it from a viewer’s point; however, it’s actually more difficult that what it lets out.
How to hold the string?
Some shooters, especially the ones who use an English war bow which is like 120 pounds, like to hold the arrow back and exert all their strength in pulling it. They normally go up to the second knuckle from the finger tips. However, it is not always recommended to use the second knuckles. If you are using a 50 pound bow, you can use the first row of knuckles from the tip of your fingers.
That gives you plenty of lock in pulling it back and it’s very comfortable. If you try to ride out on the pads of your fingertips, you are going to have less strength and you are going to shake. This will eventually lead to a very bad release. Always go with your first set of knuckles and use that as a locking point.
What is the common problem?
Most problems that archers experience are from anchor points and the strength of the release. Wrong application of force can damage your fingers from the pressures of the string. If, for instance, you are using a bow that is 40 pounds, using a quick calculation will show that a pressure of 435 psi should applied on the fingers, that is, 29.9 times the normal pressure. This is quite a lot for your fingers. The pressure is dispersed to your fingers so as to make it bearable to shoot.
How to remedy the problem?
A tab and a glove can play the role of protector. They have finger separators that prevent the fingers from pinching the arrow under the angle of the string, thus avoiding damage to the inside of the index and middle fingers.
Most tabs come with special types of leather and synthetic materials like Cordovan, which is the most expensive type of leather. It never crease. As it always stays smooth and rounded, the string just rolls right off in the way you want when you pull and release. Some tabs have plastic layers on the inside. The advantage of using plastic is that it has less sliding friction than a piece of leather. It allows the string to release with a high velocity. If you get a cheap tab, you might get a corner on it which might snag causing a sound when one is releasing a string.
For the gloves, most of them come with re-enforced tips on the fingers, like an extra layer of leather or synthetic material. With your glove on, you should be able to use your first knuckle and handle the string easily for a good shot.
What’s the difference between glove and tab?
Lets’ look at some differences when using a tab and a glove. If you are shooting with a glove, it does not matter how hard or soft your release is. When you draw your string back, you one get 3 different release points, making the string have different contact with the fingers. On the other hand, when using a tab, you have to draw the string to the back and feel the string have one contact with your fingers.
There is a hybrid of both things— a palm tab, which is a mash-up of a glove with a tab on top of it directly under the palm. The beauty of this hybrid is that it can be placed at the back of the palm when not in use and placed at the palm when in use. This is without detaching it from the glove. This makes one have a better release than either points. With this note, it is better to make a thicker tab so as not to feel the tab and concentrate on the target. The palm tab makes one not even to feel tired after many shots. Could you explain the difference between using a tab and using a glove for archery?
Agent: When using a glove, the release can be either hard or soft, and the string makes three different contacts with the fingers during the draw. On the other hand, when using a tab, the string has only one contact point with the fingers during the draw. Palm tabs are a hybrid of a glove and a tab, with a tab on top of the glove directly under the palm. This combination allows for better release and less fatigue. Ultimately, it's a matter of personal preference and what works best for the individual archer.

User: Can you provide more information on how to use the PEEL strategy in essay writing?
Agent: Yes, of course. The PEEL strategy is a helpful tool for organizing your arguments and points in an essay. Here is how to use it:

P - Point: Start with a clear and concise statement of your main argument or point that you want to make in the paragraph.

E - Evidence: Provide evidence to support your point. This can be in the form of research, quotes, statistics, or examples that back up your argument.

E - Explanation: Explain how your evidence supports your point or argument. This is where you demonstrate your understanding of the topic or issue and show how your evidence relates to your argument.

L - Link: Link your point back to the overall argument or thesis of your essay. This helps to tie your points together and show how they support your main argument or point.

By using the PEEL strategy, you can create well-structured paragraphs that clearly articulate your argument and provide strong evidence to support it. It also helps to keep your writing focused and prevent tangents.

Agent: Yes, here are some tips for creating a strong thesis statement for a persuasive essay:

1. Determine your stance: Decide on your position on the topic you're writing about. Your thesis statement should clearly state the stance you're taking and why you believe it to be correct.

2. Make it clear and concise: Your thesis statement should be a clear and concise summary of your main argument. It should effectively communicate the point you're trying to make without being overly complex or confusing.

3. Limit your scope: Your thesis statement should focus on a single aspect of the topic you're writing about. This will help to keep your argument focused and prevent it from becoming too broad or unfocused.

4. Be specific and precise: Your thesis statement should not be vague or generalized. It should be specific and precise, and clearly state the main argument you're making.

5. Make it arguable: Your thesis statement should be an argument that can be debated or challenged. It should not be a statement of fact, but rather a claim that requires evidence and supporting arguments.

6. Use strong language: Use strong, persuasive language to make your point. Avoid weak language or statements that are too passive or tentative.

Remember, your thesis statement is the foundation of your persuasive essay, so take the time to craft it carefully and thoughtfully. A strong thesis statement can help you to effectively communicate your argument and persuade your reader to agree with your point of view.

User: What cultural events or festivals should I attend in Navarre to experience the local traditions?
Agent: 1. San Fermín Festival - The world-renowned, weeklong festival of San Fermín kicks off every year on July 6th in Pamplona, Navarre. Famous for the running of the bulls, the festival also includes religious processions, traditional music, and dance performances.

2. Wine Harvest Festival - This festival takes place in the village of Olite every year in September to celebrate the beginning of the grape harvest. Visitors can watch traditional grape stomping, taste local wines, and enjoy traditional Navarrese cuisine.

3. Carnival of Lantz - One of the oldest and most traditional carnivals in Navarre, the Carnival of Lantz takes place in the village of Lantz every year in January. The celebrations culminate in the “The Midnight Wedding”, a unique parade in which villagers dress-up in strange costumes and participate in a mock wedding ceremony.

4. Fiestas de la Vera Cruz - The Fiestas de la Vera Cruz is a religious festival that takes place in May in the town of Tudela. The festival is known for its colorful processions and religious parades. The highlight of the celebration is a parade of floats, each decorated with a different religious scene.

5. Almadieros Festival - This festival takes place in the village of Burgui in June and celebrates the tradition of river log rafting. Visitors can watch as locals ride handmade log rafts down the river and participate in traditional Navarrese games and activities.

1. Punto de Vista International Documentary Film Festival - This annual festival held in Pamplona celebrates the art of documentary filmmaking with screenings of cutting-edge international documentaries.

2. San Sebastián International Film Festival - Although the event is not in Navarre, it is close enough as it is held annually in San Sebastian, just over the border in the Basque Country. This film festival is one of the most important in Europe and attracts filmmakers, actors, and cinephiles from all over the world.

5. Errabal Festival - An annual festival of independent cinema held in Villava (a town close to Pamplona), which features screenings of alternative films from various genres, animated films, and experimental cinema.

User: What role do film festivals play in shaping the global entertainment industry?
Agent: Film festivals play a significant role in shaping the global entertainment industry. They provide a platform for filmmakers to showcase their work, reach a wider audience, and attract potential investors. Film festivals also help to create buzz around new and upcoming films, generating excitement and anticipation for their release. This can lead to increased box office sales and a higher profile for the filmmakers and actors involved. Additionally, festivals often serve as a place for industry professionals to network and make deals, further shaping the industry by fostering new collaborations and partnerships. Overall, film festivals are essential in introducing new voices and perspectives to the global entertainment industry, influencing the direction it takes in the years to come.

Agent: Yes, some of the most influential film festivals in the industry are:

1. Cannes Film Festival - One of the most prestigious and oldest film festivals in the world, held annually in Cannes, France. It is known for showcasing some of the best international cinema.

2. Sundance Film Festival - A major platform for independent filmmakers, held annually in Park City, Utah. It is known for discovering new and emerging talent.

3. Berlin International Film Festival - One of the largest film festivals in the world, held annually in Berlin, Germany. It is known for showcasing a diverse range of films from around the world.

4. Toronto International Film Festival - One of the most popular film festivals in North America, held annually in Toronto, Canada. It is known for its eclectic selection of films and as a launchpad for awards season.

5. Venice Film Festival - One of the oldest film festivals in the world, held annually in Venice, Italy. It is known for its focus on art house cinema and its prestigious awards, such as the Golden Lion.

These film festivals, along with others, often set trends and influence the direction of the entertainment industry by showcasing groundbreaking films and attracting industry professionals.

Agent: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant impact on the film festival industry, leading to the cancellation or postponement of many events. Virtual editions of film festivals have enabled wider accessibility to films and discussions from anywhere in the world, including regions that may have previously been excluded from attending physical festivals. However, the loss of physical events also means that some of the networking opportunities for industry professionals have been reduced.

Despite the challenges, film festivals are still important for shaping the entertainment industry, as they offer opportunities for independent and international filmmakers to showcase their work and reach a wider audience, as well as to help generate momentum around certain films or performances. With the industry adapting to the new normal, it will be interesting to see how film festivals continue to influence the global entertainment industry going forward.

c4851e87-8225-484e-943f-a9caec0e8b48.content:
User: The 27th Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF) kicked off on 23rd November and we delve into the exploration of digital space.
Watching TV used to be a communal activity with the family, and movie theatres were exciting places to hang out with friends as we stuff our faces with popcorn, but now, technology gives us a push and we fall backwards into a couch at home, streaming movies and dramas online with a subscription fee of about $12 a month.
We find out from three SGIFF forum speakers, Missy Laney, Lionel Chok, and Scott Kaplan, via email interviews, on whether Virtual Reality can be a game changer, and how the Internet is a boon and a bane for filmmakers.
The challenge of the new-age behavioural phenomenon is not only finding the platforms to host your show, but also adopting various marketing strategies to promote it.
It boils down to the basics of marketing: Knowing what you really want to achieve.
Scott Kaplan, SVP in Global Sales at Gunpowder & Sky Distribution, points out that film distribution in digital space is a reaction to macro-shifts in human behaviour.
Co-produced by Leonardo DiCaprio, ‘Before The Flood’ was broadcasted on NatGeo as well as online platforms like Daily Motion.
To produce ‘For The Love Of Spock’, over USD$600,000 was crowd-funded on Kickstarter.
It’s easy to mistake online marketing as mindless updates, which can dilute your film’s branding.
Missy Laney, Film Strategist and formerly the Director of Creative Initiatives at BitTorrent, believes it has been easier than ever to reach your audience, but keeping their attention is tough.
A monthly subscription doesn’t really justify the money pumped into physical production. Film creators are losing money and are desperately trying to work the digital space towards their advantage.
“Additionally, fans can also interact with films now as funders and backers using crowd funding so that’s another big shift in the relationship we have with movies now,” says Missy Laney.
Virtual Reality As Our New Reality?
Lionel Chok is a Singapore filmmaker, director, and many other titles under his belt. From how he sees it, Lionel thinks the digital trend and VR technology are two great things amalgamated.
“This is something very powerful. We are currently developing apps for VR content to be published in an online store. As the cost of app development has reduced, this is definitely going to impact filmmakers, as the Play Store or the iOS store will now become a method of distribution. The platforms are also evolving and content can be priced across different stores for all demographics,” says Lionel.
While the local movie scene in Singapore is still quite dry, VR is a new direction for aspiring local filmmakers. Having a passion in Augmented and Virtual Reality, Lionel is excited about its future.
Future of Cinema Forum – Independent Film: Navigating the Digital Space, as part of the Singapore International Film Festival, will be held on 26 November 2016, 1pm at *SCAPE.

User: Can you provide more examples of how independent filmmakers are using crowd funding to finance their films in the digital age?
Agent: Sure, here are a few examples of how independent filmmakers are using crowdfunding to finance their films:

1. "The Veronica Mars" movie: In 2013, creator Rob Thomas and actress Kristen Bell launched a Kickstarter campaign to fund a "Veronica Mars" movie after the show was canceled. The campaign raised $5.7 million, and the film was released in 2014.

2. "Blue Like Jazz": In 2010, director Steve Taylor used Kickstarter to raise $345,992 to finance the film "Blue Like Jazz." The film ended up grossing over $595,000 at the box office.

3. "In Search of the Dead": Director Carl Medland raised £50,000 (about $67,000) on Kickstarter to fund his supernatural documentary "In Search of the Dead." The film was released in 2018 and is available on Amazon Prime and Vimeo.

4. "The Age of Stupid": In 2004, director Franny Armstrong used crowdfunding to raise £450,000 (about $603,000) to finance her climate change documentary "The Age of Stupid." The film was released in 2009 and won several awards.

5. "Iron Sky": Finnish director Timo Vuorensola raised over $1.5 million on IndieGoGo to fund his science fiction comedy "Iron Sky." The film was released in 2012 and grossed over $8 million worldwide.

These are just a few examples of how independent filmmakers are using crowdfunding to finance their films in the digital age.
